conjecture_tested: every finite remainder Hankel determinant has a positive single-edge asymptotic C_r exp(-alpha_r t) with faster remainder, source-derived without RH
rank_one_counterexample: the remainder localizer contains the extracted endpoint feature c(t,h)=exp(t/4)(exp(h/4)-1), so D_1 grows rather than decays; its exponent is alpha_1=-1/4
off_axis_obstruction: without RH, a least-real-part conjugate shell contributes exp(-sigma t) times a trigonometric polynomial; it need not have a positive limit under any real exponential renormalization
coefficient_circularity: positivity of the Vandermonde-square coefficient requires real sampled bases and positive grouped weights, which is the spectral conclusion rather than unconditional source input
disposition: reject the conjecture as stated; rank one is false and the higher-rank positive single-edge claim silently assumes the real spectral ordering it seeks to prove
surviving_scope: conditional on RH or independently proved reality and noncancellation of the leading shell, fixed-rank renormalized asymptotics remain valid and useful for certification
acceptance_test: A replacement must formulate the leading shell before assuming real rates, allow finite trigonometric shell sums, and derive phase cancellation or reality from source identities rather than declaring C_r positive.
